title: SimulationMaxxing: How we ship agents 20× faster — Aman Gupta (Nubank) + Shreya Rajpal (Snowglobe)

summary: Aman Gupta (Principal ML Engineer, Nubank AI Core) and Shreya Rajpal (CEO & Co-founder, Snowglobe by Guardrails AI) present how Nubank uses simulation-generated evaluation data to ship AI customer-support agents 20× faster. Nubank, the leading digital bank in Latin America with 135 million customers and $5B+ quarterly revenue, deploys five AI agents in production for customer support. The central thesis is that eval data—not metrics—is the primary bottleneck for agent development. While metrics (LLM-as-judge classifiers, auto-optimization) have a working playbook, generating eval data remains unsolved because each data point is a multi-turn trajectory with internal tool calls and consistent state—far more complex than single-turn QA data. Current approaches (manual authoring and production traces) are slow or risk testing on real users. Snowglobe addresses this by wrapping an agent via SDK with no code changes, mocking tools, and generating thousands of grounded multi-turn conversations from persona and use-case inputs. Results include 80% expert agreement that simulations produce usable data, one agent's tNPS doubling, SSR improving by 4% in one case, regressions caught before production, and the ability to short-circuit A/B tests by running many variants through simulation before a single production test. The talk closes with three takeaways: generate eval data in simulation, close the sim-to-real gap with offline/online human review metrics, and recognize that self-improving agents come down to aligned metrics plus reliable data generation.
whyItMatters: The talk presents a cohesive framework where simulation-based eval data generation, tool mocking, and the ship-observe-simulate loop work together to solve the agent evaluation data bottleneck. Multi-turn agent trajectories make traditional eval data generation (manual authoring, production traces) impractical at scale, while LLM-as-judge classifiers handle the metrics side of evaluation. Snowglobe's zero-code-change SDK wrapping and tool mocking enable grounded simulations that produce usable data (80% expert agreement), addressing the sim-to-real gap through offline/online human review. Together, these concepts form a self-improving agent loop where aligned metrics (tNPS, SSR) and reliable data generation enable continuous improvement at production scale (135M users, five agents), compressing release cycles from weeks to hours and enabling safe A/B test short-circuiting and pre-production regression detection.
temporalContext: The talk was recorded at the AI Engineer World's Fair conference (July 2026) and published on YouTube on July 29, 2026. Snowglobe was announced as a Guardrails AI product in August 2025, approximately one year prior. The referenced KDD 2026 paper was published on arXiv on June 7, 2026. Nubank's Q1 2026 quarterly revenue crossed $5 billion. Research was conducted as of August 23, 2026. At the time of the talk, five AI agents were in production at Nubank serving 135 million customers across Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia.
takeaways: Generating eval data in simulation rather than waiting on production data lets Nubank ship agents 20× faster.

Snowglobe points its SDK at an agent with no code changes, mocks tools, and generates thousands of grounded multi-turn conversations from persona and use-case inputs.
Simulation derisks changes by catching regressions before production and protecting self-service rate; one agent's tNPS doubled and SSR improved by 4% in one case.

concepts.name: Multi-turn agent trajectories
concepts.explanation: Complex evaluation data points consisting of multi-turn conversations with internal tool calls and state that must remain consistent throughout. Each trajectory is far more complex than a single-turn QA pair.
concepts.importance: Core concept explaining why agent eval data is fundamentally harder to generate than structured ML data or single-turn QA data.

concepts.name: LLM-as-judge classifiers
concepts.explanation: Using LLMs as automated judges for evaluating agent outputs, with alignment to human judgment. Part of the metrics playbook that already has a working methodology including auto-optimization.
concepts.importance: Represents the solved side of evaluation; paired with simulation-generated data for complete eval pipelines.

concepts.name: Synthetic data generation for evaluation
concepts.explanation: Producing grounded, multi-turn synthetic conversations with consistent state and mocked tools for agent evaluation, replacing manual authoring and production traces.
concepts.importance: The talk's central innovation; provides scalable, safe, and parallelizable eval data generation for agent development.

concepts.name: Sim-to-real gap
concepts.explanation: The discrepancy between simulation-generated data and real production data. Must be closed via offline and online human review metrics to trust simulation results.
concepts.importance: Critical quality concern; 80% expert agreement demonstrates simulation data is usable, but the gap must be actively monitored and measured.

concepts.name: tNPS (transactional NPS)
concepts.explanation: Per-interaction customer satisfaction metric used to evaluate agent quality in production. One agent's tNPS doubled thanks to simulation and robust evals.
concepts.importance: Primary success metric for Nubank's AI agents; demonstrates the real-world impact of simulation-based evaluation.

concepts.name: SSR (self-service rate)
concepts.explanation: Percentage of customer interactions resolved without human intervention. Must be protected when improving tNPS; simulation caught regressions and in one case improved SSR by 4%.
concepts.importance: Operational metric that creates a tradeoff with tNPS; simulation helps manage this tradeoff safely.

concepts.name: Self-improving agent loop
concepts.explanation: The principle that agents can continuously improve when paired with aligned metrics and reliable data generation, creating a virtuous cycle of ship, observe, evaluate, simulate, and optimize.
concepts.importance: Closing conceptual framework of the talk; ties together metrics, data generation, and simulation into a unified improvement architecture for enterprise agents.

concepts.name: Grounded simulations
concepts.explanation: Simulations that produce consistent, realistic data—personas with addresses, credit card numbers, tone, and account data—rather than random synthetic conversations. The Maria Souza example demonstrates a fully grounded persona.
concepts.importance: Distinguishes Snowglobe's approach from naive synthetic data; grounding ensures simulation data is usable for real-world evaluation, validated by 80% expert agreement.

concepts.name: Simulation-based evaluation pipelines
concepts.explanation: Generating test and evaluation data through simulated multi-turn conversations rather than waiting on production data or manual authoring. The talk frames this as the key engineering innovation that enables 20× faster agent shipping.
concepts.importance: Central to the talk's thesis; simulation-based eval data generation replaces slow manual authoring and risky production traces with a scalable, reproducible pipeline.

concepts.name: Tool mocking in agent systems
concepts.explanation: Replacing real tool implementations with mocks during simulation so that agents can be exercised against thousands of scenarios without real side effects. Snowglobe identifies necessary tools and dynamically mocks them.
concepts.importance: Enables safe, reproducible simulation of agent-tool interactions at scale without affecting production systems.

concepts.name: Zero-code-change SDK integration
concepts.explanation: Integration pattern where the Snowglobe SDK wraps an existing agent without requiring modifications to agent code, lowering adoption barriers.
concepts.importance: Teams can adopt simulation-based eval without refactoring existing agent infrastructure, accelerating deployment.

concepts.name: Ship-observe-simulate release loop
concepts.explanation: An iterative release methodology: ship agent to production, observe behavior, build robust evals with automated prompt optimization, simulate variants, optimize the agent harness, and ship again. This compresses release cycles from weeks to under a day.
concepts.importance: Provides a structured, repeatable methodology for continuous agent improvement that dramatically reduces iteration time.

concepts.name: A/B test short-circuiting via simulation
concepts.explanation: Running multiple agent variants through simulation before launching a single production A/B test, instead of running five or six sequential production experiments.
concepts.importance: Reduces production risk, experimentation cost, and time-to-decision by pre-filtering variants through simulation.

concepts.name: State consistency in multi-turn systems
concepts.explanation: Maintaining consistent state (user identity, account data, persona attributes such as address and credit card details) across multiple conversation turns and tool calls within a single simulation.
concepts.importance: Fundamental engineering challenge that makes agent eval data generation harder than single-turn QA; without consistent state, simulation data is not usable for evaluation.

concepts.name: Pre-production regression detection
concepts.explanation: Using simulation to identify and prevent regressions—particularly drops in tNPS or SSR—before they reach production users.
concepts.importance: Protects production metrics and customer experience by catching issues in simulation, derisking agent changes at 135M-user scale.

sections.title: Opening and Nubank at a glance
sections.summary: Shreya and Aman introduce themselves and the talk topic. Aman describes Nubank as the leading digital bank in Latin America with 135 million customers, $5B+ quarterly revenue, and high NPS, making it ideal for AI agents in customer support where humans and AI collaborate.

sections.title: Main thesis and results
sections.summary: The talk's central claim: generating eval data in simulation instead of waiting on production data lets you ship agents 20× faster. Results show tNPS across five production AI agents massively improved over a few quarters, many approaching or exceeding human quality. A KDD paper is referenced.

sections.title: Why evals matter and why data is the bottleneck
sections.summary: Shreya explains evals are about metrics and data. Metrics have a playbook (LLM-as-judge, auto-optimization), but data remains unsolved. Agent data is multi-turn trajectories with tool calls and state, far more complex than structured ML or single-turn QA data.

sections.title: How teams get eval data today
sections.summary: Two current methods: manual authoring (time-consuming, requires hand-planning state and trajectories) and production traces (free but tests on real users, blocks parallel experiments). Both are painful for different reasons.

sections.title: Simulations short-circuit the release timeline
sections.summary: Aman explains that changing an agent harness takes hours, offline evals take days, and production AB tests take weeks. Simulations compress the full loop to under a day, sometimes hours or minutes, by providing a simulated user instead of hand-curated or production data.

sections.title: How Snowglobe simulations work
sections.summary: Snowglobe wraps an agent via its SDK with no code changes, identifies tools to mock, takes persona and use-case inputs, and outputs thousands of multi-turn conversations with mocked tools, plus per-turn judge evaluations piped into the eval pipeline.

sections.title: Grounded simulation example: Maria Souza
sections.summary: A concrete simulated persona: Maria Souza, 34, designer, first-time credit card customer, with consistent fake address, credit card, tone, and account data. The agent successfully identifies the user, verifies the address, and returns valid mocked outputs.

sections.title: Ship, observe, simulate, repeat
sections.summary: Aman describes the self-improvement loop: ship, observe, create robust evals with automated prompt optimization (e.g., DSPy), simulate, pipe sim and real data through evals, optimize the agent harness, and ship. This enables many AB tests per agent across many agents.

sections.title: How close simulations are to real data
sections.summary: Simulation quality tracked against production data shows high correlation via evals. Human review found 80% of domain expert labels confirmed simulations produce usable data for both mature and greenfield agents.

sections.title: Derisking, SSR, and open-source model testing
sections.summary: Simulation derisks changes by catching regressions before production and catching issues that could lower self-service rate. One agent's tNPS doubled thanks to simulation and robust evals. The team short-circuits AB tests by running variants through sim before launching one production test. SSR was not compromised; in one case it improved by 4%. Simulation also enabled rapid testing of open-source models against frontier models, saving multiple weeks of effort.

sections.title: Three core takeaways and closing
sections.summary: Shreya summarizes three takeaways: generate eval data in simulation rather than relying solely on production to short-circuit release bottlenecks; close the sim-to-real gap with offline/online human review metrics; and recognize that self-improving agents in enterprise settings come down to aligned metrics plus reliable data generation. A reliable data-plus-metrics loop enables agents that continuously improve from feedback.

technologies.label: Snowglobe Simulation Engine
technologies.summary: Snowglobe is a simulation engine for AI chatbots by Guardrails AI that wraps agents via SDK with no code changes, dynamically mocks tools, and generates thousands of grounded multi-turn conversations from persona and use-case inputs. It produces judge-labeled eval datasets including preference pairs for DPO and reward models, and critique-and-revise triples for SFT. It is the central technology in the talk, enabling Nubank to ship agents 20x faster by replacing manual eval authoring and production traces with scalable simulation.
technologies.role: Central product and technology; demonstrated via SDK integration with no code changes, tool mocking, persona generation (Maria Souza example), and judge-labeled dataset output

technologies.label: LLM-as-judge Evaluation
technologies.summary: LLM-as-judge classifiers represent the metrics side of agent evaluation, which the talk describes as having a working playbook including alignment with human judgment and auto-optimization. The talk explicitly frames evals as metrics plus data, with metrics being the solved side. Paired with simulation-generated data from Snowglobe, they form complete eval pipelines. The KDD 2026 paper confirms inter-rater agreement analysis and GEPA optimization as part of Nubank's evaluation framework.
technologies.role: Supporting methodology; represents the solved metrics side of evaluation that pairs with Snowglobe's simulation-generated data

technologies.label: Ship-Observe-Simulate Release Loop
technologies.summary: The ship-observe-simulate loop is an iterative release architecture where teams ship agents to production, observe behavior, build robust evals with automated prompt optimization, simulate variants, optimize the agent harness, and ship again. This compresses release cycles from weeks to under a day, sometimes hours or minutes, and enables A/B test short-circuiting and pre-production regression detection. The loop is the engineering methodology that contextualizes how Snowglobe simulations integrate into the broader agent development lifecycle at Nubank.
technologies.role: Engineering methodology framework; structures the talk's narrative around how simulation integrates into production agent development cycles

technologies.label: Multi-turn Agent Trajectory Data Generation
technologies.summary: Multi-turn agent trajectory data generation is the core problem domain the talk addresses. Each eval data point is a multi-turn conversation trajectory with internal tool calls and state that must remain consistent throughout, far more complex than structured ML data or single-turn QA. This is the unsolved bottleneck that Snowglobe's simulation engine solves by generating grounded, stateful conversations with mocked tools, replacing slow manual authoring and risky production traces.
technologies.role: Problem domain; explains why agent eval data generation is fundamentally harder than traditional ML data or single-turn QA, motivating the need for simulation
